features.title: authSession runs on an async StorageAdapter
features.description: StorageAdapter { get, set, remove } returns promises. The web passes a localStorage adapter, and an extension can pass chrome.storage.local.
steps: Unit test: an in-memory adapter round-trips persist/read/clear
Unit test: an adapter that throws on get/set does not crash the caller, and reads come back as null
npm run build (client) passes — erasableSyntaxOnly
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-19 by authSession.test.ts (16 tests). DESIGN DEVIATION from spec P1 step 2, taken on purpose: the adapter is async, but authSession keeps an in-memory cache, so the getters stay SYNC. initSession() fills the cache before React mounts (main.tsx; .then is a style choice — Vite 7's default target does support top-level await, and an earlier comment claiming otherwise was corrected in P2). adapter.subscribe feeds other contexts' writes into the cache. This avoided pushing await into axios, socket handshakes and first render (R4). Writes update memory synchronously and persistTokens can be awaited; refreshOnce awaits it (R3). The throwing adapter reads as signed out, and the lazy localStorage lookup keeps a blocked store from crashing at startup. npm run build passes.

features.title: Refresh coordination unchanged by the async move
features.description: refreshOnce() still coalesces, still picks up a token another tab already rotated (accessAtStart), and endSession still fires only on 401/403.
steps: Test: two concurrent callers produce exactly ONE POST /auth/refresh
Test: refresh answers 401 → endSession fires and the tokens are cleared
Test: refresh answers 500 or the network drops → session kept and tokens intact
Test: storage already holds a newer access token than the one at start → no refresh call made
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-19. Tests cover: one refresh for two callers; 401 ends the session; 500 and network failures keep it; adopting another tab's token; waiting for the initial storage read before deciding there is no refresh token. Mutation check: removing each guard (coalescing, await ready, adopt, cache-before-notify) turns exactly its own test red.

There is no loading-state redesign: the cache is filled before render, so the initial state is right from the first frame.

features.title: P1 browser close-out
features.description: Spec P1 exit, observed in a real browser.
steps: login → reload → still logged in
two tabs, access token expired in both, both fire a request → neither is logged out, and the server sees no reuse alarm
revoke the session from another browser → the next call gets 401 and lands on /login
client CI suite + npm run build + typecheck green
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-19 with checks/p1-browser.mjs on the rig (API :3013, Vite :5199, Chrome for Testing 131): 8/8, then 5/5 on a rerun. In 5 race rounds with both tabs expired, the refreshes were [B:200, A:401] every time, both tabs stayed on /projects, and the token was renewed. Revoke-all from another login sent the next call to /login. FAILURE CASE observed: with the adopt branch removed, BOTH tabs ended at /login (the loser's endSession clears the shared store), so the check detects the regression. Client lint, typecheck (tsc -b), vitest 141/141 and build are clean. RESIDUAL, not reproduced: the loser's 401 could arrive before the winner has persisted (during the claim/issueSession window). The old code had the same exposure, and it was not seen in 5/5 rounds. The extension avoids it by construction, because its service worker is the only refresher (X2).

features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-20. Parity: 2 requests (fetch with X-Apexops-Key: 9 events; sendBeacon on unload: 1 event), identical apart from timestamps; same page errors. esbuild absWorkingDir is pinned: output embeds module paths, and a build from the repo root differed from one inside the package. Found when the drift test failed from root. Target es2018 (object spread native); v1 was ES5 by hand, which no supported browser needs. END-TO-END 2026-09-20 (checks/sdk-e2e.mjs, driving the server's own /sdk/test page on the rig, project sprint2-demo): 14/14. The served v1.js is the generated one. The SDK's flush was accepted (202, 3 events). console.error, the uncaught TypeError and the unhandled rejection each landed on their own issue in Postgres (#332-#334). The page's loop ran all 7 steps: ingest → issue → resolve → recur (regressions: 1) → alert fired (unread 1 → 2) → reopened (reopenCount 1). FAILURE CASE: serving a v1.js that cannot read data-project gives 10/14, with no flush and all three counts unchanged. /sdk/demo was not run separately; it loads the same script the same way.
